verdict: IS THE PROTEIN CHAIN WIRING, OR JUST DEGREE? The prompt for this was a fair objection to a number I reported: '99% of scorable knockouts are a node in the protein chain' says nothing about whether those nodes have edges. Measured properly the two layers differ sharply -- PPI degree among the 378 scorable knockouts has median 74 with only 3 at zero, but COMPLEX degree has median 6 and 97 knockouts (26%) have NO complex edge at all. The complex layer -- the ingredient credited for the ensemble gain and weighted 2x above PPI by the pre-registered config -- is missing for a quarter of knockouts, and '99% coverage' concealed it. THE DECISIVE TEST IS NOT COVERAGE BUT A DEGREE-PRESERVING NULL, because a walk on any realistic graph drifts to hubs and hubs are the well-studied, frequently-moving genes; this project already measured a PPI enrichment at 35x against a uniform null that collapsed against a degree-matched one. Three nulls were run with the identical pipeline, 20 resampled graphs each. REAL graph MARKOV-P recall@50 = 0.4725. NULL A (binomial, same edge count, degree and wiring both destroyed): 0.1274 +- 0.0081, z=+42.4. NULL B (degree-preserving configuration model, every node keeps its exact degree): 0.1516 +- 0.0070, z=+46.1, p<=0.048. NULL C (complex layer rewired, real PPI kept): 0.3616 +- 0.0089, z=+12.5. THE WIRING IS REAL: the chain beats the DEGREE-PRESERVING null by +0.3209 (+46.1 sd), so holding hubness exactly fixed and randomising only who-binds-whom destroys the advantage. That is the control this project's own history demanded, and it passes. It also clears the binomial null comfortably (+42.4 sd), as any working method must. NOW THE CORRECTION, AND IT OVERTURNS WHAT THIS PROJECT CREDITED FOR THE GAIN. The layer ablation reads: PPI alone 0.4729, complex alone 0.4005, BOTH 0.4725. PPI ALONE IS AS GOOD AS BOTH (0.4729 versus 0.4725) -- the complex co-membership layer, which the previous module called 'the new ingredient' and whose weight the pre-registered config set to 2x PPI, ADDS NOTHING once PPI is present. NULL C must be read against PPI-ONLY, not against the full graph: rewiring the complex layer scores 0.3616, which is BELOW PPI-only's 0.4729, so what NULL C shows is that INJECTING WRONG complex edges actively harms, NOT that real complex edges help. Those are different claims and conflating them would have turned a redundancy into a discovery. The honest attribution is that the working ingredient is the TWO-STEP WALK ON PPI; the complex layer's apparent benefit in the earlier train-set sweep (0.4909 without, 0.4996 with) did not replicate here. Knockouts has complex edges: n=281, recall 0.5212. Knockouts ZERO complex edges: n=97, recall 0.3304. BY PPI DEGREE QUARTILE: degree Q1 0.382 (n=103), Q2 0.435 (n=88), Q3 0.543 (n=95), Q4 0.549 (n=92). WHAT BOUNDS THIS: stub matching preserves degree exactly only before cleanup; dropping self-loops and duplicate pairs retained 99.1% of edges, which slightly LOWERS null degrees and therefore biases in the real graph's favour -- so a real-graph win over NULL B is an upper bound on the wiring effect. Degree-preserving rewiring also cannot destroy the coarse component structure or the fact that a knockout gene is its own node, so those are shared between real and null and are not what is being tested. With R=20 replicates the smallest attainable empirical p is 0.048, so p is reported as a bound. Deterministic given seed 0.
